newsitem.title: UK: Low wheat stocks seen adding to price volatility.
newsitem.headline: Low wheat stocks seen adding to price volatility.

text.p: Low global wheat stocks are likely to continue for some years to come and increase price volatility on world markets, the International Grains Council (IGC) said in its latest monthly report on Thursday.

The IGC forecast a rise in world wheat stocks to 104 million tonnes at the end of the 1996/97 crop year, 3.0 million tonnes higher than the previous estimate and the lowest since 1980 except for last year.

"The low level of carry-over stocks is likely to be a feature in later years," said Bill de Maria, the IGC's assistant executive director, adding that what was important now was production in the current season.
"The market is now operating without that huge amount of carry-over stocks (as in past years)," he told Reuters.
In its report, the IGC said a "significant rebuilding" of global wheat stocks was expected.

"Perhaps the main lesson is that with lower levels of stocks, price volatility increases, and current production prospects assume greater importance in assessments of world supply and demand for wheat," it said.
It said higher prices had lured farmers to expand production rapidly, with the essential advantage of favourable weather, and that extra availability had again affected prices.
De Maria said a relatively small shift in total supplies could have a quite pronounced effect on world price trends.

"Even though the growth in total availabilities of wheat in relation to global consumption is relatively small, it has already been sufficient to have had a pronounced influence on the course of international prices for wheat," the IGC said.
